newsitem.title: UK: NWE straight-run fuel falls after crude slip.
newsitem.headline: NWE straight-run fuel falls after crude slip.

text.p: European low sulphur straight-run fuel oil traded lower on Wednesday after crude futures fell sharply, forcing the seller to cut his asking price by $3 a tonne, traders said.
A cargo of low sulphur straight run was bought by a U.K.-based major from an Irish refiner at $99 a tonne fob after IPE futures came off by as much as 35 cents a barrel.
The seller had raised his asking price for the 0.7 percent material since Friday -- partly supported by crude's gains -- to reach as high as $102 at tonne but buying interest at that number was thin.
"We finally have a deal. The seller finally came to my number after crude fell," the buyer said. Wednesday's deal compared with a cargo sold out of Scandinavia on Monday at $108 cif.

Traders said that two sellers will be showing cargoes at the beginning of July, with one saying $100 a tonne fob will be a good number for his 0.7 percent material. Better quality material is offered in the $103/$104 region.
